title: Divine Judgment and Nadir Shah’s Advance on Lahore

blocks.text: The poem argues that the mass persecution of the Khalsa created such an outcry that it reached the divine court itself. Heavenly judgment now turns against the Mughal order that had tormented the Sikhs and prepares the way for a devastating invader from the northwest.

In that frame, Nadir Shah reaches Lahore while Zakariya Khan is forced into humiliating submission and heavy payment. The invasion is presented as punishment for tyranny, not merely as another military episode in imperial politics.

At the same time the turmoil opens roads and supply lines to Sikh action. The Singhs begin striking traffic along the Kabul-Delhi road, using the confusion of empire to challenge the very state that had tried to exterminate them.
